news.title: DISAPPOINTING FINISH! Nigeria's Future Eagles End FIFA U-15 World Cup Campaign in 76th Position After Panama Defeat
news.lede: Nigeria’s Future Eagles concluded their campaign at the 2026 FIFA U-15 World Cup and Festival in Baku, Azerbaijan, with a disappointing 2-1 defeat to Panama in their final classification encounter, finishing 76th in the overall standings. Sports247 reports that the result brought an underwhelming tournament experience to an end for the Nigerian youngsters, who struggled to secure consistent results despite showing moments of determination throughout the competition. The Future Eagles entered their final classification fixture hoping to end their campaign positively after suffering a heartbreaking penalty shootout defeat against Chile. However, Panama emerged victorious with a 2-1 scoreline, leaving Nigeria unable to secure 75th position.

news.title: U15 Football World Cup: Luxembourg finish 68th in first-ever World Cup appearance, above France
news.lede: The Luxembourg U15 squad concluded its U15 World Cup campaign in Azerbaijan with a 68th-place finish, following a 5-3 defeat to Scotland in its final game. The Luxembourg Football Federation (FLF) U15 squad finished in 68th place at the U15 World Cup in Azerbaijan, marking the first time a Luxembourg national football team has participated in a World Cup. news.title: Ghana take on Japan in FIFA U-17 Women's World Cup Quarter-Final - Preview
news.lede: The Black Maidens face a stern test when they take on Japan in the quarter-finals of the FIFA U-17 Women's World Cup Morocco 2026 on Sunday, November 1, 2026, at the Mohammed VI Football Complex - Pitch 1 at 3:00 PM. Ghana advanced in dramatic fashion, beating Argentina 5-4 on penalties after a 1-1 draw in the Round of 16. Jessica Appiah gave Ghana an early lead from Cynthia Obinsrewuo's assist, before Mercedes Diz equalised late after Hajara Adam had been sent off for a second booking with 13 minutes to go. The Black Maidens held their nerves in the shootout, converting all five penalties with Appiah scoring the winner to claim the Player of the Match award.

news.title: Boycotts, bans and no-shows: Notable World Cup absentees
news.lede: The first World Cup was hosted by Uruguay in 1930 and featured 13 teams, just four of which were from Europe: France, Belgium, Romania and Yugoslavia. The paucity of European teams wasn't due to a boycott but largely had to do with funds being short during the Great Depression and the difficulty of traveling such a long distance by sea. It would be linked to a boycott at the next World Cup. Italy both hosted and won their first World Cup in 1934.

news.title: Men's World Cup: Mexico's most creative football pitches
news.lede: On the southern outskirts of Mexico City, amateur teams meet on a very unique football pitch every Sunday. Known as the "Field of the Gods," it is perched inside the extinct Teoca volcano and situated a breathtaking 2,700 meters (8,800 feet) above sea level. The pitch was created by the nearby community more than 60 years ago and is a source of local pride. Cars above, sports below: this pitch in Mexico City's colorful Las Aguilas neighborhood gives people the space to play soccer beneath a highway overpass.

news.title: Malaysia kick off FIFA U-15 World Cup campaign with 3-1 win over Dominica
news.lede: Malaysia took a 2-0 lead through Aqheef Haiqal Koko's opening goal in the 12th minute before Anas Suffiyan Arif doubled the advantage seven minutes later. KUALA LUMPUR : The national Under-15 squad opened their Group H campaign in the 2026 FIFA Under-15 World Cup and Festival with a 3-1 victory over Dominica in Baku, Azerbaijan today. Dominica reduced the deficit through a penalty in the 28th minute, but Amirul Faris Azlan sealed the win for coach P. Maniam's side with a third goal in the 39th minute.
